packets.headline: Fall Open House set for Saturday, Nov 14
packets.briefing: Clarkson University holds its next Fall Open House on Saturday, Nov 14, per @clarksonuniv on Nov 10. Prospective students can tour campus, see hands-on learning, and get a feel for life as a Golden Knight. Registration is open now. Watch for turnout and any follow-up admissions deadlines tied to the visit.

packets.headline: Third Wheel Pottery named 2026 Business of the Year
packets.briefing: The Potsdam Chamber named Third Wheel Pottery Studio its 2026 Business of the Year, per @potsdamchamber on Nov 10. Owner Robin Wolpin built the studio into a place to try pottery and learn together, including Senior Discount Mondays, and her volunteers make about 100 handmade bowls a year for the Empty Bowls fundraiser at the 1844 House. The studio will be celebrated Thursday, Nov 12, at the Chamber's Annual Dinner and Awards at The Stables at Windy Point. Watch for photos and remarks from the dinner.
packets.location: The Stables at Windy Point, Potsdam

packets.headline: Youth Nordic ski rentals open; apply by Nov 20
packets.briefing: The Potsdam Public Library and SUNY Potsdam's Wilderness Education Program opened sign-ups for the Youth Nordic Ski Program, per @potsdampubliclibrary on Nov 10. The program offers season-long cross-country ski rentals for children ages 3 to 17, running November 2026 through April 2027, for $100 per child, with scholarships for families receiving SNAP benefits. Applications are due Friday, Nov 20, and equipment is limited. Watch whether demand outruns the available gear.

packets.headline: Co-op reopens at 10 AM tomorrow after repairs
packets.briefing: The Potsdam Food Co-op finished its flooring repairs and plans to open one hour late tomorrow, Wednesday, Nov 11, at 10 a.m., per @potsdamcoop on Nov 10. A freezer failed beyond repair and damaged the subfloor, forcing Monday's closure; the Co-op is buying a replacement, so freezer options may be limited in the meantime and staff can check backstock. Watch for the replacement install and a return to normal hours.

packets.headline: Bears sweep Saint Joseph for first wins of the season
packets.briefing: The SUNY Potsdam women's hockey team swept its first regular-season weekend, per @potsdam_hockey on Nov 10. The Bears rallied for a 5-2 win over the University of Saint Joseph on Friday, Nov 6, the first victory of head coach Rachel Corbett's tenure, then blanked the Blue Jays 5-0 on Saturday, Nov 7, behind freshman Campbell Hegerty's two goals and junior captain Maddy Ferguson's shutout. The sweep evened Potsdam at 2-2. The Bears open SUNYAC play at home against Cortland on Friday, Nov 13.
packets.location: University of Saint Joseph, West Hartford, CT

packets.headline: Clarkson blanks RPI 4-0 behind Soderwall shutout
packets.briefing: Clarkson men's hockey beat RPI 4-0 on Saturday, Nov 7, at Cheel Arena, per @clarksonalumni on Nov 10, with alumni in New Mexico among those watching. Senior goaltender Shane Soderwall made 31 saves for his second shutout of the season as the Golden Knights improved to 5-4-1 overall and 2-0-0 in ECAC Hockey play. The win capped a weekend that also included a 6-2 win over Union on Friday. Clarkson has next weekend off before returning to league play at Cornell and Colgate just before Thanksgiving.

packets.headline: Ceramic tile workshop added to Tauny fall lineup
packets.briefing: Tauny Center added a late fall workshop where participants make their own ceramic tile with instructor Aryn Rivers, per @thetaunycenter on Nov 10. Students choose from real botanicals to press a design into the tile, and glazes and firing are provided by Third Wheel Pottery Potsdam. No date was named in the post, so check Tauny's listings for the session time before planning to go.

packets.headline: MTA rail chief tours Alstom and Micro Bird in Plattsburgh
packets.briefing: The North Country Chamber hosted MTA Chief of Rolling Stock Jessie Lazarus in Plattsburgh on Monday, Nov 9, per @ncountrychamber on Nov 10. Lazarus, joined by MTA Senior Director David Frazier, toured Alstom and Micro Bird and sat down for a lunch roundtable with local companies, economic developers, and officials. The visit reflects the MTA's standing as a major customer for the region's transportation equipment cluster. Watch for any follow-up orders or announcements from the Plattsburgh plants.

packets.headline: Alexandria Bay welcome sign nearly beautified
packets.briefing: The project to beautify the Alexandria Bay welcome sign is down to finishing touches, per @7newswatertown on Nov 10. The post gives no completion date or details on what the work involved. Watch for the finished sign and any village announcement.

packets.headline: Thompson Park golf lease proposal amended
packets.briefing: The person looking to lease the Thompson Park Golf Course in Watertown has amended her proposal, per @7newswatertown on Nov 10. The post does not say what changed or name the prospective lessee. Watch for the city's response and the next step in the lease process.

packets.headline: Watertown meal program drops county funding to feed all
packets.briefing: Community Meals at Emmanuel in Watertown gave up $149,000 in Jefferson County funding so it can serve anyone who needs a meal, per @7newswatertown on Nov 9. The program serves weeknight meals in the basement of Emmanuel Congregational Church on Hamilton Street, and coordinator Steph Russell said the data collection required for county money took time away from helping people and was not doable for the amount received. As of Nov 1 the program is completely self-funded, and under the old funding someone who was not homeless might not have been allowed to eat. Russell believes the program will survive even with money tight. Watch for community donations and whether the county responds.

packets.headline: Parishville candlemakers chase $300K at NYC holiday markets
packets.briefing: Adirondack Fragrance Farm of Parishville is aiming for $300,000 in sales at New York City holiday markets, per @7newswatertown on Nov 9. The company, led by CEO Yen Maine, is selling for the first time at the Grand Central Holiday Fair, a 35-vendor show running through Christmas Eve, after loading a van with thousands of candles, bars of soap, and perfume sets. Starting Dec 1 it will also hold a space at the Columbus Circle Holiday Market, which it attended last year. Watch whether the NYC run hits the $300,000 mark.

packets.headline: Good fall weather pays off for road crews
packets.briefing: Good fall weather has paid off for North Country highway crews, per @7newswatertown on Nov 9. The post gives no specifics on which projects finished early or saved money. Watch for end-of-season project updates from county highway departments.

packets.headline: Watertown airport free parking could end
packets.briefing: Watertown International Airport has always offered free parking, but Jefferson County could start charging for it, per @7newswatertown on Nov 9. The post does not say what rates are under consideration or when a decision might come. Watch for county discussion and any public comment.

packets.headline: Santa breakfast and dinner set at Gran View
packets.briefing: Santa is coming to Winter Wonderland at Gran View on the River in Ogdensburg, per @granviewontheriver on Nov 10. Breakfast with Santa runs Sunday, Dec 6, from 9 a.m. to noon, with a buffet and a visit with Santa for $24 ages 12 and up and $21 for ages 3 to 11. Dinner with Santa follows Friday, Dec 18, from 5 to 8 p.m., ordering from the regular dinner menu. Reservations are required for both. Watch for sellouts as December approaches.
packets.location: Gran View on the River, Ogdensburg

packets.headline: Remington Museum open Veterans Day, 11 AM-4 PM
packets.briefing: The Frederic Remington Art Museum in Ogdensburg will be open from 11 a.m. to 4 p.m. on Veterans Day, Wednesday, Nov 11, per @remingtonmuseumofart on Nov 10. The museum pitched it as a place to spend time with art for anyone with the day off. Watch for holiday attendance and any Veterans Day programming.

packets.headline: SLC Arts seeks sponsors for school-break art programs
packets.briefing: SLC Arts is seeking community sponsors for its February and April school break art programs for young people in St. Lawrence County, per @slcartsny on Nov 10. The goal is $10,000 to support eight weeks of youth programming, including teaching artists and supplies, with the February and April sessions ending in a community celebration on Saturday, April 17, featuring a mini art exhibition and live performance. Sponsorship inquiries go to Erica at the Arts Council. Watch whether the $10,000 goal is met before the February session.

packets.headline: Saints upset No. 17 Union 2-1 for first win
packets.briefing: St. Lawrence men's hockey knocked off No. 17 Union 2-1 on Saturday, Nov 7, at Appleton Arena, per @slu.saintsnation on Nov 10. Luke Posthumus scored his first collegiate goal and Gunnar Thoreson added the game-winner in the first period, while Cameron Smith held the lead in goal. It was the Saints' first win of the season and their first over a nationally ranked opponent since the 2024-25 campaign. The Saints are off next week before visiting Colgate on Friday, Nov 20.

packets.headline: Robillard and Finnegan take Liberty League weekly honors
packets.briefing: St. Lawrence football players Luke Robillard and Jack Finnegan earned Liberty League weekly awards, per @slu_fb on Nov 10. The post does not name which awards each player won. Watch for the official Liberty League announcement with the details.

packets.headline: Kat and Sierra share Roo of the Week honors
packets.briefing: SUNY Canton women's basketball named Kat and Sierra co-Roos of the Week after a strong opening weekend, per @suny_canton_wbb on Nov 10. The post gives only first names and no game details. Watch for the Roos' next results to see whether the strong start holds.

packets.headline: Snow potential rising late this week in northern NY
packets.briefing: The potential for snow is rising later this week in Vermont and northern New York, per @weather.ben on Nov 10. A round of valley rain and mountain snow is likely through Thursday, with a potential flip to snow in the Champlain Valley after sunset Thursday, and lingering snow showers are possible through Friday. Watch the forecast updates as the system gets closer.

packets.headline: Showers possible today, highs in the mid-50s
packets.briefing: A slight chance of showers is expected later today, with highs topping out in the mid-50s, per @7newswatertown on Nov 10. Watch for the late-week system bringing a better chance of snow.

packets.headline: Adirondack lakes show stress as algal blooms spread
packets.briefing: The Adirondack Council published a new blog on what is happening in Adirondack lakes, per @adirondackcouncil on Nov 10. Low-nutrient lakes still offer clean drinking water and a thriving tourism economy, but harmful algal blooms are a sign of stress, and the Council argues it is far cheaper to protect lakes that are just starting to show stress than to rescue ones already impaired. Watch for the Council's specific lake findings and any policy push that follows.

packets.headline: Co-op closed today for repairs
packets.briefing: The Potsdam Food Co-op is closed today, Monday, Nov 9, for repairs, per @potsdamcoop. The post says only that the closure is for 'some important repairs' and gives no reopening time, so anyone who normally shops the Co-op on Mondays should plan around it today. There is no word yet on whether the closure extends past today.

packets.headline: Cortez earns all-tournament honors in title run
packets.briefing: SUNY Potsdam senior guard Nicholas Cortez was named to the Lafrance Hospitality All-Tournament Team, per @potsdambears on Nov 8. Cortez averaged 24.5 points on 51.5 percent shooting across two games at UMass Dartmouth, scoring 19 in Friday's 75-73 season-opening win over the hosts and a career-high 30 in Saturday's 95-82 championship loss to Emerson. The Bears split the weekend to open 1-1 and travel to SUNY Poly on Tuesday for a 5:30 p.m. game.

packets.headline: SigEp cleans up Route 11 for the year
packets.briefing: The brothers of SigEp NYX spent the weekend on their annual highway cleanup along Route 11 in Potsdam, per @sigep_clarkson on Nov 8. The Clarkson fraternity chapter does the cleanup every year as part of its community service, keeping its adopted stretch of the highway clear. It is a routine service outing, but it is the kind of steady town-gown work that keeps showing up from Clarkson chapters.

packets.headline: Bears rake leaves across the village for annual service day
packets.briefing: SUNY Potsdam student-athletes spent Sunday on their annual Leaf Raking Day, per @potsdamsaac on Nov 8. Bears from across the athletic department fanned out to rake leaves at village residents' houses, then headed to Bayside Cemetery to clean up there as well, turning a rainy morning into a sunny afternoon of community service. The cross country and track teams and the women's hockey team were among those posting from the day. It is a yearly tradition the department looks forward to each fall.

packets.headline: Chamber welcomes five new Potsdam members
packets.briefing: The Potsdam Chamber of Commerce welcomed five new members, per @potsdamchamber on Nov 8. The new members are StoneWear Creations, NOLA ON MAIN, Spirit & Soul Wellness, CABIN, and Riverhill Trailer Rentals, introduced to the wider North Country in a segment on ABC50. The Chamber is giving all five a warm welcome as they join the local business community. It is a small sign the Potsdam business roster keeps growing heading into the holidays.

packets.headline: '2AM' opens Friday at SLC Arts
packets.briefing: SLC Arts has a new original play on stage this weekend, per @slcartsny on Nov 8. '2AM,' an original play by Nick Attanasio that ran off-Broadway, comes to Potsdam with local actors, including Emily Reed-Fecketter as Shelly, for performances Friday, Nov 13 and Saturday, Nov 14 at 7 PM, doors at 6:30. The diner-set comedy follows Matthew, Anthony, and Brian through their relationship woes at 2 a.m. Tickets are $24, with a pay-it-forward option to help cover actor pay. The play is part of a busy SLC Arts week that also includes a jazz group and digital collage classes.

packets.headline: CPS closes fall season with Cohen night
packets.briefing: The Community Performance Series closed out its Fall 2026 season with a soulful night of Leonard Cohen music from Perla Batalla, per @cpspotsdam on Nov 8. The crowd was on its feet singing 'Hallelujah' together for the encore. The series says a Spring 2027 lineup is coming, along with news of a Summer Musical 27. The fall closer leaves Potsdam's main concert series on a high note heading into winter.

packets.headline: Rain clears out, highs near 50
packets.briefing: Rain showers will come to an end through the day across the Watertown area, per @7newswatertown on Nov 9. Highs stay around 50. It is a damp start to the week that dries out as the day goes on, with no snow in the immediate picture for the Potsdam area.

packets.headline: Woman killed by taxiing plane at Wilmington airfield
packets.briefing: A 67-year-old Wilmington woman was killed Friday afternoon at Catalano Airfield in Wilmington, per @7newswatertown on Nov 8. Pamela M. Haselton was photographing a 1943 Aeronca L3 single-engine aircraft with a tripod-mounted camera on the runway when the plane, which had just landed and was taxiing toward a hangar, struck her at about 3:47 p.m. on Nov 6. The pilot, 77-year-old James J. Catalano of Wilmington, reported not seeing Haselton or the camera. Lifesaving measures were attempted at the scene, but Haselton was pronounced dead. New York State Police are investigating alongside the Federal Aviation Administration and the National Transportation Safety Board, and the investigation remains ongoing.

packets.headline: Search on for missing Massena man
packets.briefing: The community is being asked to help find a missing Massena man, per @7newswatertown on Nov 8. The post carries no name, description, or last-seen details in its caption, so anyone with information should check the station's full report for the details that matter. The ask itself is the signal: a neighbor is missing and police are looking for the public's help. Watch for updates from the station as the search develops.

packets.headline: Council releases 45th State of the Park report
packets.briefing: The Adirondack Council released its 45th annual State of the Park report, per @adirondackcouncil on Nov 8. The report looks at federal rollbacks of environmental protections and growing pressure on New York's landmark environmental laws, and at the decisions and decision makers shaping the Park's wild lands, clean waters, and rural communities. The Council says the moment calls for renewed advocacy, broader engagement, and stronger conservation leadership. The full report is linked in the Council's bio.

packets.headline: Last Free Fishing Day of 2026 is Wednesday
packets.briefing: Wednesday, Nov 11 is the last Free Fishing Day of 2026, per @lakeplacidadk on Nov 8. No freshwater fishing license is needed anywhere in New York that day, so anyone can grab a rod and fish the region's waters for free. Lake Placid's picks around town include the West Branch Ausable River, Upper and Lower Cascade Lakes, Lake Placid itself, and the South and North Forks of the Boquet River. The day falls on Veterans Day, so it is a free outing that lines up with a day off for many.

packets.headline: Bonus Bucks put $34,000 into local farms
packets.briefing: GardenShare's Bonus Bucks program wrapped another successful year of helping families buy local, healthy food, per @gardenshare_slc on Nov 8. Participants' own spending on local food added up to more than $34,000 in economic impact for local farmers and producers across St. Lawrence County. About 90 percent of Bonus Bucks participants do not qualify for traditional assistance, which is why the program says it is crucial for middle-income families. GardenShare is running a fall fund appeal to make 2027 even bigger.

packets.headline: 1890s Newton Falls mill photo surfaces in Clifton
packets.briefing: This week's North Country at Work photo shows young male workers posing in front of paper rollers and a paper cutter at the Newton Falls Paper Mill, circa 1890-1900, per @ncpr on Nov 8. The print can be viewed in person at the Town of Clifton Museum, and more photos of the Newton Falls mill are in the station's online archive. It is a small window into the paper industry that once anchored the Clifton area. The weekly series keeps pulling local history out of the archives and into public view.
packets.location: Town of Clifton Museum, Newton Falls

packets.headline: Flannel Fest takes over downtown Canton Saturday
packets.briefing: Flannel Fest returns to downtown Canton on Saturday, November 14, per the Facebook event listing found November 9. The celebration of local businesses runs during each shop's own business hours, with stores along Main Street featuring flannel-themed specials as holiday shopping gets underway. Organizers are asking shoppers to wear flannel and spend locally, calling each dollar spent downtown an investment in the businesses that support local teams, events, and organizations. The event is centered at 60 Main Street in Canton, and 70 people had marked themselves interested as of this morning.

packets.headline: Exceptional Art Club returns to Ogdensburg Dec 5
packets.briefing: The St. Lawrence County Exceptional Art Club holds its next session Saturday, December 5, from 1:30 to 3:30 p.m. at St. John's Episcopal Church in Ogdensburg, per the Facebook event listing found November 9. The club is a welcoming, inclusive art experience designed for children with higher support needs, ages 2 through high school, in a sensory-aware environment where kids explore creativity at their own pace. Each session offers adaptive, process-focused art activities meant to build self-expression, confidence, and joy, with no prior art experience needed, and families and caregivers are welcome to support participation. Registration is through the ticket link on the event page or at encompassrec.com.
packets.location: St. John's Episcopal Church, 500 Caroline St, Ogdensburg

packets.headline: Four Golden Knights alumni skate at IIHF Women's Worlds
packets.briefing: Four Clarkson women's hockey alumni took the ice at the IIHF Women's World Championships, per a post in the Clarkson Golden Knights Hockey Fans group on November 8. Haley Winn is skating for Team USA, while Sara Manness, Renata Fast, and Nicole Gosling are representing Canada. The post shared game-day entrance clips of all four, a reminder of how heavily Clarkson alumni feature on the world stage. It is a proud weekend for the Golden Knights program back in Potsdam.

packets.headline: Coakley's hardware becomes worker-owned co-op
packets.briefing: Coakley Home and Hardware, a 124-year-old North Country business with a store in Canton, became a worker-owned cooperative last week, per Sun Community News on November 6. The workers closed on the purchase of the company on October 30, 2026, and the business now counts 30 worker-owners and growing. Diane Cullen, who has worked at Coakley's since she was 16, is among the new owners after 37 years with the company, and Agnes White serves as a worker-owner and CEO of the Canton store. The company, founded in 1902, also has a location in Saranac Lake, and the new owners say they are already starting to act like owners.

packets.headline: Thankful for Seniors gift-card drive ends today
packets.briefing: Today, Monday, November 9, is the last day to contribute to the St. Lawrence County Office for the Aging's Thankful for Seniors drive, per the Watertown Post's November 7 daily brief. The 13th annual drive collects gift cards and contributions toward buying them for older adults in the county's home-delivered meal program, with cards planned to reach clients by Thanksgiving. Contributions can be mailed to the Office for the Aging at 80 State Highway 310 in Canton, and the office can be reached at 315-386-4730 for current arrangements.
packets.location: Office for the Aging, 80 State Highway 310, Canton

packets.headline: Watertown council hears Thompson Park golf lease plan tonight
packets.briefing: Watertown's City Council is due to hear a proposal to lease the Thompson Park golf course at its work session tonight, Monday, November 9, per the Watertown Post's November 7 daily brief. The sole proposal comes from Andrea Doane and would pay the city $3,000 a month from April through October next season. The presentation is part of the council's consideration of alternatives for operating the course; it is not an approved lease, and any deal would still need council approval and a state law change. The work session starts at 7 p.m. in Council Chambers at City Hall.

packets.headline: Gendebien concedes NY-21 race to Constantino
packets.briefing: Blake Gendebien conceded the NY-21 congressional race to Anthony Constantino on Friday, November 6, per the Watertown Post's November 7 daily brief. Gendebien said the remaining ballots would not change the outcome, closing out the contest for the North Country's House seat. The concession follows Election Day on November 3 and the count of the remaining ballots through the week. Constantino now holds the district seat heading into the next Congress.

packets.headline: Weekend sweep capped by Soderwall shutout
packets.briefing: Clarkson men's hockey swept its ECAC opening weekend at Cheel Arena, per @clarksonmhockey on Nov 7. The Golden Knights beat Union 6-2 on Friday, then blanked RPI 4-0 on Saturday behind senior goalie Shane Soderwall, who stopped all 31 shots for his second shutout of the season and fourth of his Clarkson career. The sweep lifts Clarkson to 5-4-1 overall and 2-0-0 in ECAC play. The Knights now get a weekend off before returning to league play at Cornell and Colgate just before Thanksgiving.

packets.headline: Evans powers 6-2 road win at Union
packets.briefing: No. 9 Clarkson women's hockey kept its road trip rolling with a 6-2 win at Union, per @clarksongoldenknights on Nov 7. Junior Janelle Evans led the way with two goals and two assists for a season-high four points and a plus-5 rating, earning ECAC Three Stars of the Night honors. The Golden Knights won the road game in Schenectady to stay hot in early ECAC play. Watch whether Evans keeps this scoring pace as the trip continues.

packets.headline: Robitaille wins it in OT for 2-0 Bears
packets.briefing: SUNY Potsdam men's hockey stayed unbeaten with a 2-1 overtime win over Nazareth at Maxcy Ice Arena, per @potsdambears on Nov 7. Freshman Owen Robitaille scored his first career goal with 27 seconds left in overtime, finishing a two-on-one feed from Owen Watson, who had also scored the Bears' power-play opener. Junior goalie Luciano Chinappi made 35 saves for his third career win as Nazareth outshot Potsdam 36-22. The Bears move to 2-0 and open SUNYAC play against SUNY Canton on Nov 13.

packets.headline: Kids play 'Going Nuts' hits the museum stage Nov 22
packets.briefing: The North Country Children's Museum in Potsdam has a new kids' stage production on the calendar, per @nccmuseum on Nov 8. 'Going Nuts: A Play for Kids and Families' runs Sunday, Nov 22 at 2 PM on the museum stage, and admission is included in the price of admission or membership. The story follows Nelson the gray squirrel and his Grandpa Quercus hunting for buried acorns, with the audience helping the squirrels find the stash. It is a family daytime event two weeks out, worth a note for anyone planning a Potsdam weekend with kids.

packets.headline: Potsdam Chamber opens membership drive
packets.briefing: The Potsdam Chamber of Commerce is out recruiting members, per @potsdamchamber on Nov 8. The pitch is aimed at both new businesses and longtime ones: membership brings member spotlights and community events that put a business in front of more people, plus chances to meet other local owners and swap ideas. Joining or renewing runs through the Chamber's website. It is a routine membership push, but it signals the Chamber is actively building its roster heading into the holiday shopping season.

packets.headline: Saints host Vassar in Liberty League final today
packets.briefing: No. 7 St. Lawrence men's soccer plays for a title today, per @stlawrencesoccer on Nov 8. The Saints host Vassar in the Liberty League Final at 1:30 PM on Sandy MacAllaster Field in Canton, after beating Skidmore 4-1 in the semifinal behind a Baker Diaz brace. The post is a straight call for support from Saints fans, with the team asking the home crowd to turn out. A win would send the Saints into the NCAA tournament as league champions.

packets.headline: Robillard's two fumble returns power Senior Day rout
packets.briefing: St. Lawrence football closed its home schedule with a 38-7 Senior Day win over Buffalo State at Weeks Field, per @saabski on Nov 7. Luke Robillard returned two fumbles for touchdowns as the Saints' defense starred in the first half, forcing five turnovers and blocking two punts, with Jack Finnegan adding a 97-yard kickoff return. The Saints honored 19 seniors before their final home game. St. Lawrence moves to 3-6 overall and 2-4 in the Liberty League ahead of its finale next Saturday at Rochester.

packets.headline: Saints take 2-1 win over Union for 5-point weekend
packets.briefing: St. Lawrence men's hockey capped its weekend with a 2-1 win over Union at Appleton Arena, per @slumenshockey on Nov 7. The Saints took five of a possible six points on the weekend, after tying RPI 2-2 on Friday and winning the shootout for the extra point. Goalie Cameron Smith made 31 saves on 32 shots for his first win of the campaign, earning ECAC Three Stars of the Night honors. The result keeps the Saints' early ECAC form trending up heading into next weekend.

packets.headline: Saints shut out RPI 4-0 to rebound
packets.briefing: St. Lawrence women's hockey rebounded with a 4-0 shutout win over RPI on Saturday in Troy, per @slusaintshockey on Nov 7. Ryla Haslam scored twice, with goals also from Sonia Mehta and Kendall Doiron, and Kassidy Lawrence made 11 saves in net. The win came a day after the Saints fell 5-4 at Union, so the shutout steadies the weekend. The Saints return home after splitting the road trip.

packets.headline: Roos hockey sweeps Saturday, men stay perfect at 4-0
packets.briefing: SUNY Canton hockey swept Saturday at home, per @rooathletics on Nov 7. The men's team beat Elmira 2-1 in overtime at Terry Martin Arena: freshman Nolan Wytrykusz tied it with just over five minutes left in regulation for his first collegiate goal, and Joshua Rumolo won it 3:30 into overtime, lifting the Roos to 4-0-0. The women's team blanked MCLA 8-0, with Isabella Paswaters scoring twice and six teammates adding one goal each. Both programs are rolling early, and the men's unbeaten start is the one to watch.

packets.headline: McRobbie sets blocks record as Roos win 77-50
packets.briefing: SUNY Canton women's basketball closed its Ohio trip with a 77-50 win over Kent State Tuscarawas, per @rooathletics on Nov 7. Junior Kathleen McRobbie set the Roos' Division III era career blocks record with 82, passing the previous mark of 81 held by Samantha Dayter '24, after recording four blocks in the game. Sierra Pabo led the scoring with 17 points and seven assists, while McRobbie added 11 points and nine rebounds as four Roos finished in double figures. The record is the headline here: a program mark falling in just the second game of the season.
packets.location: Kent State Tuscarawas, New Philadelphia, OH

packets.headline: Chamber rounds up Small Business Saturday deals
packets.briefing: The North Country Chamber of Commerce is building its Small Business Saturday roundup, per @ncountrychamber on Nov 8. The Chamber is collecting local holiday specials, exclusive discounts, gift-card deals, and giveaways into one place so shoppers can find them and keep holiday spending local. Participation is free, and businesses can submit their offer at the link in the Chamber's bio. Small Business Saturday falls Nov 28 this year, three weeks out, so the roundup will fill in over the coming days.

packets.headline: Leonard Cohen tribute at Hosmer Hall tonight
packets.briefing: Perla Batalla brings her tribute 'A Letter to Leonard' to Hosmer Hall at SUNY Potsdam tonight, Saturday, Nov 7, at 7:30 PM, per @cpspotsdam on Nov 7. The show is the 47th McElheran Visiting Artist event and falls on the anniversary of Leonard Cohen's passing, with Batalla offering songs, stories, and poetry from an artist who worked closely with Cohen. Walk-up tickets are available in the Hosmer lobby starting at 6:30 PM, and tickets are also at cpspotsdam.org. It is the headline arts date on Potsdam's weekend calendar.

packets.headline: Golden Knights open ECAC play with 6-2 win over Union
packets.briefing: Clarkson men's hockey beat No. 17 Union 6-2 on Friday night at Cheel Arena, per @clarksonmhockey on Nov 7, with the result confirmed by Clarkson Athletics. Justin Cote and Bryce Sookro scored twice each as the Golden Knights opened ECAC Hockey play with their biggest offensive outburst of the young season. The win moves Clarkson to 4-4-1 overall and 1-0 in league play. The Knights host RPI tonight at 7 PM at Cheel. Watch whether the offense carries over against RPI.

packets.headline: Ouellette stars as Bears open with 5-1 win over Elmira
packets.briefing: SUNY Potsdam men's hockey opened its season with a 5-1 win over Elmira on Friday night at Maxcy Ice Arena, per @potsdambears on Nov 7, with the result confirmed by Potsdam Athletics. Freshman Travis Ouellette scored twice in his first career game, including his first goal at 16:19 of the first period, and added an assist; Owen Watson also scored. The win opens Potsdam's 50th season of intercollegiate hockey. The Bears host Nazareth today at 4 PM at Maxcy. Watch for the result from the second game of the homestand.

packets.headline: Bears open basketball season with 75-73 win

packets.headline: What North Country voters were thinking on Election Day

packets.briefing: SUNY Canton cross country wrapped its conference championship Saturday at Fortin Park in Oneonta, per @rooathletics in the Nov 1 sweep. Brielle Smith paced the Canton women for the sixth time in as many races and won the SUNYAC Elite 20 award, which honors the student-athlete who reaches the pinnacle of competition at the conference championship level. Aiden Bartlett led the Canton men for the third time this season. Watch for Smith's regional prospects, since an Elite 20 award pairs competitive and academic standing in a way that draws postseason attention.

packets.headline: Schoner sets Canton career goals record
packets.briefing: SUNY Canton men's hockey has a new D-III era career goals king, per @rooathletics in the Nov 1 sweep. Senior Niko Schoner scored 6 goals with 2 hat tricks on the weekend, and his 38th career goal broke the previous program mark of 35 held by Joe Deveny '19. Schoner recorded his second hat trick in as many days and the fourth of his career, while Colton Alexander scored twice as the Roos completed a weekend sweep at Misericordia with a 7-4 win on Saturday. Watch whether Schoner keeps extending a record he now owns outright as the season continues.

packets.headline: Warming trend ahead after a chilly Halloween
packets.briefing: Halloween itself is bright but chilly, with a warmup on the way, per @mynbc5 in the Nov 1 sweep. Temperatures climb again in the first week of November and may reach 70, with a next widespread rain chance ahead. The swing from a chilly Halloween to possible 70s within days is the kind of whiplash that matters for outdoor plans and the last fall yard work. Watch for the rain timing, since a widespread round would be the first real soaker in a dry stretch.

packets.headline: Halloween night at Cheel: Knights host Niagara
packets.briefing: Clarkson men's hockey is back at Cheel Arena tonight for a Halloween matchup against Niagara, with puck drop at 4 PM and a costume contest for fans in the stands, per @clarksonmhockey in the Oct 31 sweep. A home date on Halloween night is a natural draw in Potsdam, and the costume contest gives the game a community feel beyond the hockey itself. Niagara comes in as the opponent for a Saturday night that doubles as a holiday event. Watch for the crowd and the contest to set the tone as much as the score.

packets.headline: Bears make history in SUNYAC second round
packets.briefing: The Potsdam Bears men's soccer team is playing in the second round of the SUNYAC tournament for the first time ever, per @potsdamsoccer in the Oct 31 sweep. Kickoff is 11 AM at Red Dragon Field in Oneonta against SUNY Oneonta, with $5 admission and a livestream on the SUNYAC athletics site or app for fans who cannot travel. A first-ever second-round appearance is a program milestone, and it keeps Potsdam's fall postseason alive into the weekend. Watch whether the Bears can extend a historic run on the road.

packets.headline: Liberty League Championships at Bard
packets.briefing: Clarkson cross country heads to Bard College in Annandale-on-Hudson today for the Liberty League Championships, one of the final races of the season, per @clarkson_xc in the Oct 31 sweep. The women's race starts at 11 AM and the men's race follows at noon. Championship day is the measuring stick for a season's work, and a strong team showing here closes the fall on a high note. Watch for individual and team placements as results come in.

packets.headline: Golden Knights take down Harvard 4-3
packets.briefing: The Golden Knights beat Harvard 4-3, per @clarksongoldenknights in the Oct 31 sweep. A win over Harvard carries weight whatever the sport, and a one-goal result suggests a tight, hard-fought game rather than a comfortable night. The post gives no scorer details, so the headline stands on the final score alone. Watch for a fuller recap to fill in how the Knights closed out a 4-3 win.

packets.headline: Halloween night at McDuff's, no cover
packets.briefing: McDuff's Pub in Potsdam is marking Halloween night with no cover charge, a 21-and-over crowd, a costume contest, and a karaoke DJ, per @mcduffspub in the Oct 31 sweep. The Market Street pub is pitching a night built for lingering: deals, costumes, and karaoke rather than a single headliner. For downtown Potsdam on Halloween, that is the late-night option after the family events wind down. Watch for the costume contest to be the centerpiece of the evening.

packets.headline: Poetry evening at the Downtown Artist Cellar in Malone
packets.briefing: North Country Public Radio is hosting an evening of poetry at the Downtown Artist Cellar in Malone, per @ncpr in the Oct 31 sweep. Featured poets Elena Dickinson, Michael Nerney, Jennifer Giambruno Gordon, Esthela Calderon (with translations by Steven F. White), and Erica Kelso will read, and an open mic will follow, with Ethan Shantie emceeing. Wine and snacks will be available, and copies of NCPR's poetry collection Into the Same Sky will be on sale. The post names no date, so the timing is unconfirmed from this post alone. Watch for NCPR to confirm the evening's date before making plans.

packets.headline: Ghost stories by candlelight in Canton
packets.briefing: Ghost stories filled Grace Episcopal Church in Canton on a recent evening ahead of Halloween, per @ncpr in the Oct 31 sweep. Adults and kids in costume gathered by candlelight in the old stone church to tell and hear Old Irish, Appalachian, and Adirondack folktales, from the original jack-o'-lantern to a man who stole his dead wife's golden arm. The Reverend Caroline Carson, new to the North Country from Charleston, South Carolina, put the evening together, bringing a southern storytelling tradition to a region with ghost stories of its own. The full story is on ncpr.org, reported by Richard Haller. Watch for more of Carson's community storytelling as she settles into Canton.

packets.headline: Pancake Breakfast funds 200 meals a day in Watertown
packets.briefing: The Salvation Army in Watertown serves about 200 hot meals a day in addition to helping families through its food pantry, per @7newswatertown in the Oct 31 sweep. Its Pancake Breakfast this Sunday, Nov 1, helps fund those programs, with details on the WWNY site. Two hundred meals a day is a substantial daily operation for a single city program, and a breakfast fundraiser ties community giving directly to that table. Watch for turnout on Sunday as a measure of local support heading into the winter months.

packets.headline: Henderson lands $22 million for Henderson Harbor sewers
packets.briefing: The Town of Henderson has been awarded a $22 million grant for the Henderson Harbor sewer system, per @7newswatertown in the Oct 31 sweep. That is a major infrastructure investment for a small Jefferson County waterfront community, where sewer capacity shapes both year-round homes and seasonal growth. A grant of this size removes a long-standing barrier to development and water-quality protection on the harbor. Watch for the town to lay out a construction timeline and what the project means for harbor residents.

packets.headline: McBride seeks reelection in Jefferson County District 6
packets.briefing: McBride is seeking reelection to the Jefferson County Legislature in District 6, per @7newswatertown in the Oct 31 sweep. The post, dated Oct 30 on the WWNY site, is a straightforward campaign announcement with no platform details in the caption itself. County legislature races decide the local decisions closest to home, from budgets to county services, and District 6 voters will see this name on the ballot. Watch for campaign details and any challengers to emerge as the election approaches.

packets.headline: Roos open men's hockey with a 9-1 rout
packets.briefing: SUNY Canton men's hockey opened its season with a 9-1 win over Misericordia on Friday night, per @rooathletics in the Oct 31 sweep. Niko Schoner scored a hat trick, Logan Kelly added two more, and Samuel Moshurchak contributed a goal and an assist in a statement start to the season. A nine-goal opener sets an early tone for a Roos program looking to build momentum. Watch whether the scoring depth shown here holds up once the schedule toughens.

packets.headline: SLU football Senior Day set for Nov. 7
packets.briefing: St. Lawrence football fell to Hobart on a fall afternoon in the North Country, but the Saints get one more road game and then a final home regular-season game, per @saabski in the Oct 31 sweep. Senior Day is Nov. 7 against Buffalo State with a 1 PM kickoff. A home finale gives the senior class its sendoff in front of its own crowd, and a win would close the home slate on a positive note. Watch for Senior Day details and the Saints' road result before that finale.

packets.headline: ADK warning: bear cans still required, Trap Dike icy
packets.briefing: The Adirondack Mountain Club is warning hikers to avoid backcountry nightmares this Halloween weekend, per @adkmtnclub in the Oct 31 sweep. Bear cans are still required for overnight trips through Nov. 30, the Ten Essentials belong on every hike, and the Trap Dike is a technical climb, not a hike, made even more dangerous by thin icy conditions. That warning matters as late-fall conditions arrive in the High Peaks, when a route that looks walkable can turn technical fast. Watch for conditions updates before any High Peaks trip, and treat the Trap Dike as a climb only for prepared parties.

packets.headline: SLC Arts Holiday Mixer offers $5 custom poems
packets.briefing: SLC Arts will feature poet Ryan Murphy at its Holiday Mixer on November 20, writing custom poems on the spot for $5 each, per @slcartsny on Oct 30. The mixer is the arts council's fourth annual winter gathering, and the post frames the poems as a ready-made unique gift. Pre-registration is open through the SLC Arts online shop. For Potsdam, this is the first firm date on the holiday arts calendar, and it lands a week before the downtown holiday season kicks into full gear. Watch for the full mixer lineup as November 20 approaches.

packets.headline: Chamber thanks Potsdam for Fright Night
packets.briefing: The Potsdam Chamber closed the book on Thursday night's Fright Night with a public thank-you to the volunteers, board members and Events and Festivals Committee who put it together, per @potsdamchamber on Oct 30. The post singles out Potsdam Police and the DPW, the Village for the sign and lights over Raymond Street, and students at Lawrence Avenue Elementary and A. A. Kingston Middle School for the downtown window artwork. It also credits the Haunted Hallway, candy sponsors, participating businesses and the families who turned out. The tone is a wrap, not a preview, which confirms Fright Night landed as the downtown anchor event of the Halloween week. Nothing in the post previews a next Chamber event, so the holiday calendar is the open question now.

packets.headline: Adirondack coalition forms to bolster child care
packets.briefing: Business leaders and child care advocates in the Adirondacks have formed a coalition to strengthen child care across Warren, Franklin, Clinton, Essex and Hamilton counties, per @7newswatertown on Oct 30. The post gives no names, funding figures or first projects, so the coalition reads as newly announced rather than operational. Its footprint matters for the North Country because Franklin County sits inside it, and child care capacity is a standing constraint for employers and families across the region. What to watch is whether the coalition names members, a funding ask or a first county-level initiative in the coming weeks.

packets.headline: High Peaks weekend: mild days, icy summits, early sunsets
packets.briefing: The Adirondack Mountain Club's backcountry update for October 30 through November 1 calls for partly sunny skies with a chance of rain Friday and Sunday and highs in the mid-50s at lower elevations, per @adkmtnclub on Oct 30. The warning is at altitude: summits are regularly dipping below freezing even during the day, with thick ice at higher elevations, so the club strongly urges hikers to carry trail crampons or MICROspikes. Daylight Saving Time ends Sunday, which pushes sunset before 5 PM, and the club advises setting a turnaround time and packing two light sources with extra batteries. Bear cans remain required for overnight trips in the Eastern High Peaks Wilderness. The practical read is a split weekend: pleasant trailhead weather that turns genuinely winter-like on the summits.

packets.headline: Dry weekend ahead after a meager overnight rain
packets.briefing: Northern areas picked up only a trace to about a tenth of an inch of rain overnight, with Saranac Lake recording the most at just 0.19 inches in 24 hours, per @meteorologist_allison_black on Oct 30. The post notes that any rain is welcome at this point, which points to a dry stretch that the small overnight totals did little to break. Dry weather returns through the weekend, and the next best chance for rain does not arrive until late next week. For the North Country, that means another dry, fire-aware weekend with no meaningful drought relief in sight. Watch the late-week forecast for whether that next rain chance firms up or fades.

packets.headline: Long-closed downtown Watertown building opens as haunted house
packets.briefing: Part of a downtown Watertown building that has been closed to the public for decades is open this weekend as a haunted house, per @7newswatertown on Oct 30. The post gives no address, hours or admission details, so the item reads as a teaser pointing readers to the station's fuller coverage. The hook is the building itself: space the public has not been inside for decades, repurposed for Halloween weekend. For Watertown, it adds a downtown draw to a weekend already stacked with Halloween events. The detail to confirm before sending anyone is the exact location and hours.

packets.headline: Salvation Army Pancake Breakfast returns Sunday in Watertown
packets.briefing: Watertown's Salvation Army holds its annual Pancake Breakfast on Sunday, November 1, from 8 AM to 1 PM at its State Street location, per @7newswatertown on Oct 30. Tickets are $8 for adults and $4 for children, with pancakes, French toast and all the fixings on the menu. The fundraiser supports the hot meals served daily and the food pantry, which makes it both a community breakfast and a direct funding line for the organization's feeding programs. The timing, the morning after Halloween, gives it a natural family crowd. It is one of the weekend's clearest buy-a-ticket, do-some-good options in Jefferson County.

packets.headline: Three Jefferson County legislators face challengers
packets.briefing: Three Jefferson County legislators are seeking to keep their seats against challengers, per @7newswatertown on Oct 30. The post links to the station's fuller report but names no candidates or districts in the caption itself, so the specifics sit behind the link. The item still matters as an Election Day marker: with voting days away, county legislature races are the local contests most directly shaping services and budgets. Watch the linked report for which seats are contested and whether any incumbent faces a serious challenge.

packets.headline: $9.8M for Carthage, West Carthage water system

The caption gives no breakdown of the funding source or the projects it will cover, with details behind the station's linked report. For two small Jefferson County villages sharing a water system, an award of this size is a major infrastructure event, likely touching treatment, distribution or compliance work. The figure to watch next is how the money is split between system upgrades and what, if anything, it means for local water rates.

packets.headline: Winter Wonderland at Gran View opens November 27
packets.briefing: Winter Wonderland at Gran View in Ogdensburg opens on November 27, now 29 days out, per @granviewontheriver on Oct 30. For Ogdensburg, it is an early signal that the holiday events calendar is filling in. Watch for ticket, hours and attraction details in the coming weeks.

packets.headline: Scarecrow Scuttle wraps for 2026
packets.briefing: The Arc Jefferson-St. Lawrence County has wrapped its 2026 Scarecrow Scuttle, thanking runners, volunteers and supporters for a day of fall fun for a good cause, per @thearcjslc on Oct 30. The post describes a full day from starting line to finish line with familiar faces and new friends, but gives no turnout or fundraising totals. As a fundraiser for the Arc's foundation, the Scuttle is one of the organization's community-facing events of the fall, and the wrap post closes it out with a see-you-next-year note. The open detail is the result: attendance and dollars raised, which would tell whether this year's edition grew on last year's.

packets.headline: Fright Night takes over downtown Potsdam tonight
packets.briefing: Downtown Potsdam's Fright Night runs tonight, Thursday, October 29, from 5 to 8 PM with free admission, per @potsdamchamber on Oct 29. Trunk-or-treating spans three sites -- Market Street, Market Square Mall, and the new Best Western parking lot -- with 65 participating businesses and organizations. Costume contests check in at JobsRUs on Depot Street from 5 to 6 PM, winners are announced at 6:30 PM at the BB9.3 tent, and the Wicked Witches of Norfolk perform on Market Street at 6:30 PM. Games along Raymond Street, a haunted hallway, a spooky movie in front of the Children's Museum, and tarot readings round out the evening. Watch for the downtown window art by Lawrence Avenue and A.A. Kingston students, and expect Market Street to be busy through 8 PM.

packets.headline: Halloween night at Cheel: Clarkson hosts Niagara
packets.briefing: Clarkson men's hockey turns Saturday, October 31 into a Halloween night at Cheel Arena, per @clarksonmhockey on Oct 29. The Golden Knights face Niagara at 4 PM, and fans under 14 who arrive in costume receive a free general admission ticket at the ticket office. Trick-or-treating runs during intermission around Cheel and the Boneyard. It is the kind of low-cost family night that usually fills the student section early, so arriving before puck drop is the smart move.

packets.headline: Composting drop-in at the Children's Museum Nov 21
packets.briefing: The North Country Children's Museum will host a composting and food-waste drop-in on Saturday, November 21, from 10 AM to 1 PM, per @nccmuseum on Oct 29. Visitors can make garlands from dehydrated fruit, print greeting cards with vegetable stamps, and explore the science of composting, all included with museum admission. The event is staged with Clarkson Sustainability and the Village of Potsdam, a sign of how the museum keeps pairing kid-friendly making with real local partners. Mark it as a family morning option well ahead of the holiday stretch.

packets.headline: Bears men's soccer makes program history in SUNYAC playoffs
packets.briefing: SUNY Potsdam men's soccer won its first postseason game in program history, beating SUNY Delhi 4-2 in the SUNYAC Playoffs, per @sunypotsdam on Oct 29. Thomas Wendel scored twice, Kyan Tiede added a goal and two assists, and Mason Zambrano scored once. A first playoff win is a program milestone, not just a result, and it keeps a season alive that now has a real postseason story. The Bears move on with momentum and a growing crowd behind them.

packets.headline: Bears head to Oneonta for Saturday's 11 AM matchup
packets.briefing: Potsdam men's soccer now turns to Saturday's matchup at Oneonta, with an 11 AM kickoff, per @potsdamsoccer on Oct 29. The trip follows the Bears' dominant 4-2 first-round win over SUNY Delhi, their first playoff victory in program history. Oneonta on the road is a step up in difficulty, and an 11 AM start means an early bus and a fast start matter. A win there would extend the deepest postseason run the program has ever had.

packets.headline: SLU men clinch Liberty League regular-season crown
packets.briefing: No. 4 St. Lawrence men's soccer clinched the 2026 Liberty League Regular Season Championship, per @stlawrencesoccer on Oct 29. The Saints went 5-0-3 in conference play with one game remaining, securing the No. 1 seed and home field for the postseason. They will host their semifinal on Friday, November 6 at Sandy MacAllaster Field, with the time still to be announced. Hosting the semifinal in Canton is a genuine edge in November conditions, and the road to the trophy now runs through St. Lawrence.

packets.headline: County budget would cut tax rate for 12th straight year
packets.briefing: St. Lawrence County's proposed budget maintains services while lowering the tax rate for the 12th consecutive year, per @7newswatertown on Oct 29. Twelve straight years of rate cuts is a remarkable run for a rural county, and the administrator is framing it as steady stewardship rather than a one-year windfall. The proposal still has to move through the legislature, where the details of what is maintained -- and what is trimmed -- will draw the real scrutiny. Watch for the public hearing schedule and any legislator pushback on specific lines.

packets.headline: Heuvelton picks 5 projects for $4.5 million grant
packets.briefing: Heuvelton has chosen five projects to fund with its $4.5 million downtown grant, per @7newswatertown on Oct 29. The village now faces the familiar question of what made the cut and what did not, with the full list carrying the real story for residents and business owners. A $4.5 million infusion is transformative at Heuvelton's scale, so the sequencing of the five projects -- which break ground first -- is worth tracking. The next step is the detailed project list and timelines.

packets.headline: Three deaths in under two months unsettle Brushton
packets.briefing: Three deaths in less than two months have unsettled the village of Brushton, per @wcaxtv on Oct 29. Police say a woman was found dead in her home Tuesday, and her ex-husband was found dead after a police chase more than 200 miles away. Residents are quoted saying the string of deaths makes them want to lock their doors at night. Watertown's schools serve a large Fort Drum-connected population, so transitions in and out of the district are a constant operational reality. A commissioner's visit on this topic signals state-level attention to how military-connected students are received and supported. The practical test will be whether the visit produces any change in transition support, not just the conversation.

packets.headline: Rocky Horror returns to Watertown's Strand for Halloween
packets.briefing: Watertown Lyric Theatre brings The Rocky Horror Show to The Strand, per @7newswatertown on Oct 29. The run offers 7 PM shows Thursday and Friday, a special 10 PM performance on Halloween night after trick-or-treating, and additional performances November 5-7. The Halloween-night show is the draw: a cult classic staged for a costumed crowd on the night itself. Tickets for the late show are the ones most likely to go first.

packets.headline: Warm day near 70 before a cold front arrives
packets.briefing: Today brings a warm day with highs topping out near 70 before a cold front moves through, per @7newswatertown on Oct 29. For late October in the North Country, near 70 is a gift -- and a brief one, since the front behind it will reset conditions. Outdoor plans, including Potsdam's evening Fright Night, get the warm side of the change, but anyone out late should expect the turn. Check the evening forecast before heading out in costume.

packets.headline: Fire danger stays high after a week of brush fires
packets.briefing: Fire danger remains high across Vermont and New York, with crews reporting multiple brush fires in the last week, per @mynbc5 on Oct 29. Dry conditions plus fallen leaves are a classic late-October combination, and open burning or discarded smoking materials can get away fast. The warning covers both sides of Lake Champlain, so North Country residents should treat it as local even though the post is regional. Hold off on brush burning until conditions ease and watch for any local burn advisories.

packets.headline: Adirondack Council releases 45th State of the Park report
packets.briefing: The Adirondack Council has released its 45th annual State of the Park report, per @adirondackcouncil on Oct 29. The report examines federal rollbacks of environmental protections and growing pressure on New York's landmark environmental laws, arguing the forces shaping the Park's wild lands, clean waters, and rural communities are changing rapidly. Its call is for renewed advocacy, broader engagement, and stronger conservation leadership. For North Country readers, the report is the annual scorecard on the Park's political weather, and its specific grades on decisions and decision-makers are worth reading in full.

packets.headline: ORDA fall festivals drew 64,170, up nearly 48 percent

Belleayre's Fall Festival led with 33,558, followed by Gore Mountain's Harvest Fest at 20,449, Whiteface's Oktoberfest at 6,265, and the Flaming Leaves Festival at 3,898. The events featured 211 vendor participants, including 115 local vendors, plus nearly 20,000 scenic gondola rides. The surge is a strong shoulder-season signal for the Olympic venues heading into winter, with local vendors capturing a meaningful share of it.

packets.headline: Watertown weighs nuclear option alongside solar plan for former landfill
packets.briefing: Watertown officials are considering whether to explore nuclear power at the city's former landfill while continuing to evaluate a possible solar farm there, per ClickNNY on Oct 29. The 78-acre site could support solar on about 40 acres, according to a Willdan Performance Engineering representative, with council estimates ranging from a loss of up to $151,000 a year to a gain of up to $450,000 a year. Council member Shane Garrabrant proposed pursuing nuclear as a parallel option, Doug Osborne supported further investigation, and Ben Shoen questioned whether the site has enough usable land for a nuclear facility. The city's hydroelectric contract is expected to end around 2029 or 2030, which frames the search for a new energy or revenue source. Residents near the Water Street homes have raised concerns about property values, environmental effects, and possible soil chemicals, while others said the city should decide how to use the property. The process remains in its early stages, with no action taken yet.

packets.headline: Watertown winter parking ban returns Nov 1
packets.briefing: Watertown's seasonal overnight parking ban returns November 1, barring vehicles from city streets between 2 AM and 6 AM through April 30, per ClickNNY on Oct 28. The rule, under city ordinance section 293-21c, lets Department of Public Works crews clear snow overnight, with an exception for physicians responding to emergency calls. Vehicles parked in violation may be fined and towed. The city lists free downtown municipal lots on Stone Street, State Street, Arcade Street, Court Street, JB Wise, Newell Street East and West, and Union Street for residents without driveways or off-street parking. Property owners remain responsible for clearing snow from private sidewalks and keeping fire hydrants clear. The ban is an annual marker that winter operations in Watertown are about to begin.

packets.headline: Vance visit reported for Ogdensburg Nov 2 as Blakeman plans Watertown event Nov 1
packets.briefing: Vice President JD Vance is reported to be campaigning for Republican congressional candidate Anthony Constantino in the North Country on Monday, November 2, per ClickNNY on Oct 28, updated Oct 29. The reported destination remains unclear, with reports placing the event in Ogdensburg and Rome, and the White House has not announced the visit. The Secret Service surveyed Ogdensburg International Airport, and Vance is expected to land instead at the Fort Drum military base airfield, according to a report citing the Times Union. A Constantino campaign spokesman declined to comment on the travel plans. Separately, Republican gubernatorial candidate Bruce Blakeman is scheduled to hold a free event for Jefferson County voters at 2 PM Sunday, November 1, at the Caprara Events Center on Faichney Drive in Watertown. Both appearances come just before Election Day in the closely watched New York 21st District race, so confirmation of the Vance stop is the detail to watch.

packets.headline: St. Lawrence County trail use draws conflict as study and rule debate continue
packets.briefing: St. Lawrence County's multi-use trail system is at the center of a dispute over noise, litter, environmental concerns, enforcement, and off-highway vehicle use on public roads, per ClickNNY on Oct 26. Lynda Bage and Becky Allen helped form St. Lawrence County Neighbors for Sensible OHV Standards, which has brought its concerns to county legislators several times since spring 2026. The town of Colton has reaffirmed its ban on ATVs and UTVs on town roads, while some residents display signs calling for roads to be made legal for ATV use. The county's 2026 trail rules prohibit alcohol on the trail and require registered and insured machines, helmets and eye protection, posted speed limits, and litter removal, with an annual OHV permit at $65 for the first machine. A Clarkson University study is examining how the system is used and enforced, and the trail system is marking its 20th anniversary in 2026. Senate bill S7298, which would raise ATV size limits, sits in the Transportation Committee after a January 2026 referral.

packets.headline: Bears reach postseason for first time since 2015

Organizers describe it as a huge, well-advertised show with a wide variety of participants, and crafters, artisans and direct-sale vendors are signing up now. The listing shows 150 interested and 44 going, a strong early pull for a December date. This is the furthest-east Franklin County entry on this run's radar.
